_doc: The garment reading checklist (cloth_reference.py; guide(topic="cloth_reference")): what a pattern maker, tailor, costume designer or garment artist reads off reference art, item by item, BIG TO SMALL (stage 1 silhouette and lengths, 2 fit, 3 construction details, 4 wear state and layering, 5 fabric and folds). The same list does two jobs: READ a reference into a design sheet + a target table (garment_from_reference) and CHECK a simulated garment against that table (check_garment_reference). Item keys: id; stage; kinds (garment_kb kinds, or '*' = every garment); what (what to look for, a sentence to act on); view (front | side | back | three | close: which picture shows it); region (body landmarks the focus crop is drawn round, + pad m); type: length (two image points -> a height, read ANCHORED: the fraction t along anchor[0] -> anchor[1], carried onto our body) | width (two points across -> a share of the body's own width at that height, `per`) | choice (a garment_kb detail's choices, or `choices` here) | count | bool | colour (sRGB sampled from the crop) | level (a word on `scale`); measure: cloth_reference.MEASURES name that reads our sim, or 'missing: ...' (said in the check, not judged); tolerance: mm after carrying onto our body (length), share (width), 0 = exact (choice, count, bool), deltaE (colour), steps (level); sets: the design-sheet key or pattern op that changes it. Landmarks (cloth_reference.LANDMARKS): head_top, chin, neck_base, shoulder.L/R (the shoulder point), armpit, chest, waist, hip, crotch, knee.L/R, ankle.L/R, floor, elbow.L/R, wrist.L/R. Tolerances are what a full-figure picture supports, not a factory spec (tech packs work to +-3..13 mm; a concept doesn't hold that).

items.what: The garment's overall outline from the front: boxy, straight, fitted (in at the waist), A-line / flared, tapered. Read it before anything else: it is what reads from across a room.
Where the hem ends at the centre front, against the body: for a jacket, does it cover the seat? (a classic jacket ends at the knuckles with the arm hanging, covering the seat).
The hem at centre back against the front: level, or the back longer (a shirt tail) or shorter (a jacket riding up behind).
Where the sleeve ends along the arm, against the wrist bone (long sleeves) or the elbow (short): a jacket sleeve ends at the wrist bone so the shirt cuff shows below it.

Where the hem rests: above the ankle, on the shoe's top (no break), folding once over the shoe (half break), pooling (full break). Read the front hem's height over the floor and whether the cloth folds above it.
Where the shoulder line ends: on the shoulder point (tailored), past it with a dropped seam (casual), squared by a pad or sloping with the body.
Across the chest just under the armpits, edge to edge in the front view (the tech pack's 'chest 1 inch below armhole'): close to the body (slim), a hand's room (regular), loose.
Does the garment come in at the waist (darts, side panels) or hang straight from the chest? The waist's width against the chest's.
items.sets: ops take_in on the side seams; darts

items.what: The hem's width edge to edge in the front view (bottom sweep): does it flare out from the hips or hug them?
The sleeve's width at the bicep and at the hem against the arm: a slim tailored sleeve or a full one.
From the side, do the open fronts hang straight down from the chest (good balance) or stand forward at the hem (a tent)? The hem's distance ahead of the body at the hip.
items.units: mm: the fronts' lowest edge ahead of the chest's front (+ = forward of it: a tent)
items.sets: contour sideF/sideB hem spring; front_balance; canvas bands

items.what: The width at the seat / hip in the front view: close, a little room, full.
One leg's width at the knee, edge to edge in the front view, against the leg (the cut: skinny, slim, straight, wide).
One leg's width at the hem in the front view against the shoe / ankle (it should cover the shoe's heel counter on a suit trouser, not flare past the shoe).
Where the waistband sits: at the natural waist (high), at the hip bones (mid), below (low).
The collar's type: shirt collar on a stand, band, convertible, notched lapel, peaked lapel, shawl, hood, rib, bound or faced neckline.
The lapel's width at its widest, square to the roll line, against the chest (classic 85-100 mm; slim < 70; wide > 110).
Where the collar meets the lapel (the gorge seam / notch): high (near the collarbone) or low (on the chest).
items.measure: missing: the notch's height on the sim (pattern point gorge/notch not carried into a light result)

items.what: How the front closes: buttons single-breasted, double-breasted, one button, a button stand under a lapel, a zip, a wrap, a pullover.
How many buttons on the front (count what you see; on a shirt the collar button counts separately).
items.sets: op buttons n (jacket); design table buttons (shirt)

items.what: The height of the top (waist) button: at the natural waist / a little above, where the lapels' roll ends (the break).
The shirt front's placket: a box placket (a raised band with two rows of stitching), French front (no band), hidden (fly front).
items.sets: closures front finish {over, under} (design table / garment closures entry); design.details.placket

items.what: How the sleeve ends: barrel cuff, French cuff, rib, plain hem, a jacket's hemmed sleeve with buttons.
Pockets you can see: flap, welt (jetted), patch, slant, in-seam, kangaroo, a breast welt on a jacket's left chest; or none.
A back vent: centre vent, side vents, none (back view only).
The waistband: straight, extended (a tab buttoned past the fly), contoured, elastic, faced (no band).
Is there a belt? (a strap with a buckle at the front over the waistband; loops). A belt's colour and buckle are often the brightest accent at the waist.
A pressed crease down the front of each leg (a sharp line from the waist's pleat or dart to the hem).
The fly: a zip fly with a J of stitching on the left front, a button fly, none.
Is the front worn closed (buttoned) or open (hanging free)? A suit jacket is often worn open; a dress shirt closed.
How many of the front's buttons are done up (count; on a two-button jacket: top only = 1; a dress shirt with no tie: all but the top one).
The shirt collar: buttoned to the top (under a tie) or open at the throat with the points spread on the collarbones (no tie).
items.sets: sheet tie true|false; closures collar state

items.what: Is the shirt tucked into the trousers (no shirt hem visible below the waistband) or worn out?
Which garment lies over which (skin out): shirt under jacket, shirt in trousers, jacket over trousers' waistband. Name the garment directly under this one.
At the back of the neck, how much of the shirt collar shows above the jacket collar (10-20 mm on a good fit; negative = the jacket collar covers it or stands away).
items.sets: op collar stand_height / jacket back neck; layering

items.what: How much shirt cuff shows past the jacket sleeve (10-15 mm, about half an inch).
Does the jacket collar hug the shirt collar and the neck at the back, or stand away from it (a gap you can see into)?
Do the lapels lie flat on the chest along the roll line, or stand off / buckle?
The cloth: fibre and weave as it reads (wool suiting, flannel, tweed, cotton shirting, oxford, denim, jersey, linen), its weight (light, medium, heavy) and surface (matte, sheen, nap).
The garment's colour in its LIT mid-tones (not the highlights, not the shadow), sRGB; and the pattern if any (solid, stripe, check, herringbone) with its scale.
How the cloth falls: crisp (holds its shape, few big folds: canvas, starched cotton), medium (suiting), soft (jersey, silk: many small folds clinging).

Where the folds are and how many: compression folds at the elbows and the back of the knee, tension folds from a button, a few broad gravity folds; a well-pressed garment has very few. Clean, rumpled or creased.
New and pressed, worn in (soft creases at the elbows and behind the knees), or old (shine, bagging, frayed edges).
items.measure: missing: no wear / breakdown pass on cloth yet (paint layers)
items.sets: paint layers on the garment's part
